title: chart.points
description: Estimates by category from a CSV, one row each: a dot with an optional interval whisker (or a before and after pair) and its value written beside it, against a value axis and an optional reference line; or, with `id`, a beeswarm strip of many points per category with a summary tick and one item followed across the strips. The axis stays fixed across steps, rows can appear one by one, and a missing value reads "no data", never zero.

data.description: Path to a CSV file, relative to the deck root. One row per category (one row per point, with `id`).

x.description: Column holding the category of each row (its text labels the row). Each category appears in one row only, unless `id` makes it a strip.

y.description: Column holding the estimate of each row. An empty cell shows "no data" (never a dot at zero). Changing it moves every dot to its new value; the axis covers every step's column, so it stays put.

from.description: Column holding the earlier value of each row, for a before and after pair: a hollow dot at it, a quiet connector, and the filled dot at `y`. An empty cell shows the end dot alone (no hollow dot, no connector). Setting it on a step slides each filled dot from its old value to `y` while the connector grows; the axis covers `from` at every step, so it stays put.

interval.description: A whisker from the lower to the upper column through each dot (e.g. a 95% interval). A row without both bounds has no whisker. Changing it moves the whisker ends.

x.description: d3-format spec for category labels, applied when the category column is numeric (e.g. years).

y.description: d3-format spec for value labels, ticks and the interval text.

format.description: Label formats (d3-format, localized by the deck language, so a Spanish deck gets the decimal comma). Without `y`, ticks use a fixed precision from the tick step and value labels show the value as it is.

x.description: Title of the category axis, above the category labels.

y.description: Title of the value axis, under the ticks.

axes.description: Axis titles: `x` names the categories, `y` the values. A title that appears, changes or goes fades; room for it is kept at every step, so the plot never resizes.

types.description: CSV column types, passed to the data loader. Undeclared columns are numbers only when every value looks like one.

domain.description: Fixed value axis as [min, max], used as given. An estimate outside it is an element error; an interval past it is cut at the axis end. In strips, points outside it are not drawn: a box at that end of the row counts them. Without it the axis spans `y`, `from` and the interval columns of every step, and every step's `reference`, rounded outward to tick values (zero is not forced).

shown.description: Categories to show, by name. Omit to show every category. A row that appears grows out of the reference line (else 0, else the axis start) and then draws its whisker; one that leaves does the reverse. Hidden rows keep their place. An unknown category is an element error naming it.

sort.description: Order of the rows. "none" (the default) keeps the data order; "value" orders by `y`, lowest first, and "-value" highest first; { by, order } orders by another column (ascending unless `order` is "desc"); a list of categories puts those first, in that order, and the rest after them in data order. Strips rank by their summary (the median with `summary: "none"`) and { by } reduces that column the same way. Ties keep data order and rows without a value come last, whichever way it runs. Hidden rows keep their place in the order. When it changes on a played step, every row slides to its new place; a row that appears grows in at its place. An unknown column or category is an element error naming it.

id.description: Column naming each point, for strips: with it every row is one point, and a category's rows become a beeswarm strip in its band (each point keeps its place apart from its neighbours), with a summary tick. Ids are unique within a category; the same id in several categories is the same item, which `focus` follows. A row with an empty value is not drawn (never at zero), and a row with an empty id is skipped. `from` and `interval` are not drawn in strips.

summary.description: Strips: the summary tick across each strip, at the median (the default) or the mean of all its values; "none" draws no tick. `sort` ranks strips by it (by the median with "none"), and `sort: { by }` reduces that column the same way. A change fades the old tick out and the new one in.

focus.description: Strips: one item (an `id`) followed across the strips: its dots are ringed in ink and raised, a line joins them from strip to strip in row order (skipping a strip without it), and every other dot turns the theme's dim color (never faded). An id the data does not have is an element error.

highlight.description: Category to emphasize; the other rows' dots and whiskers turn the theme's dim color and their value labels the muted color (never faded, so labels keep their contrast). Usually set with `only` so it lasts one step. An unknown category is an element error naming it.

value.description: Where the line sits on the value axis.

label.description: Text above the line, at the top of the plot.

reference.description: A dashed reference line across every row, at a value (a number) or with a label ({ value, label }), such as an average or a target. It fades in, out or across to a new value. It widens the default axis to reach it; past a given `domain` it is not drawn.
